newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM launches hectic poll tour of key state.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM launches hectic poll tour of key state.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda began a hectic tour on Tuesday of a key Indian state holding local assembly polls that could determine the future of his four-month old coalition government, his colleagues said.

Deve Gowda left the Uttar Pradesh state capital of Lucknow on Tuesday for three days of whistle-stop election meetings after spending the night with senior party colleagues, officials of his United Front alliance said.
"These elections are absolutely vital for the government in Delhi," Deve Gowda's junior minister for telecommunications, Beni Prasad Verma, told a news conference in Lucknow.
"Our future depends on them," Verma said.

Verma was speaker of the Uttar Pradesh assembly last year when the socialist Samajwadi Party, a key component of the United Front, was in power in alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) of low caste Hindus.

The alliance collapsed after the BSP ditched then-chief minister Mulayam Singh Yadav in a failed attempt to strike up a pact with the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which forced New Delhi to put the state under its direct rule.

Tens of thousands of paramilitary troops have been deployed to guard the three-phase elections that began on Monday in the violence-prone state. With 140 million people, the sprawling state is more populous than Japan or Pakistan.
Police last week clamped an around-the-clock curfew in the Moslem-majority old quarter of Lucknow, the state capital and the main base of the BJP.

The assembly polls will see Deve Gowda's fractious United Front alliance take on the Congress party, which supports his minority government in Delhi, and the BJP in a triangular fight for the state's 425-member Vidhan Sabha, or lower house.

Politicians said the polls, involving 90 million eligible voters, would test Deve Gowda's ability to ride out a challenge by the BJP, India's main opposition group which is campaigning for mid-term parliamentary polls.

"It is inevitable now that mid-term polls for parliament will be held sooner than later," BJP president Lal Krishna Advani told reporters in Lucknow on Sunday. "There are too many contradictions in this government."
Verma said relations with the Congress could improve and not worsen after former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned as its president in favour of veteran leader Sitaram Kesri last month.
"Mr Kesri is possibly the best Congress leader we can have good relations with," Verma said.

The BJP derives its major strength from Uttar Pradesh. Its campaign to build a Hindu temple at the site of a 16th century mosque there catapulted it to power in several north Indian states and made it the main opposition in parliament in 1991.

Analysts say the state, once a bastion of the Congress party which has ruled India for all but four years since independence in 1947, could boost a recent trend of coalition politics that helped Deve Gowda form a minority government in June.
On the other hand, a poll by the Times of India on Sunday predicted a possible victory for the BJP, saying the Hindu nationalists could get betwen 205 to 215 seats in the 425-seat assembly.
